problem: Vision-language models cannot effectively reason about moving targets across large-scale camera networks by integrating geographic maps and multiple video perspectives simultaneously.
approach: GTR-Bench introduces a benchmark that combines geographic and temporal reasoning with non-overlapping field-of-view videos and map context to evaluate VLMs' geo-temporal intelligence.
contribution: Benchmark shows top VLMs like Gemini-2.5-Pro achieve only 34.9% accuracy versus 78.61% human performance, revealing three key deficiencies in spatial-temporal reasoning.

problem: Current LLM development requires manual training runs with static datasets/rewards to extend model capabilities, preventing continuous discovery of diverse skills.
approach: AC/DC coevolves LLMs via model merging and tasks via synthetic data generation, discovering populations of diverse expert models in a single continuous run.
contribution: LLM populations achieve broader expertise coverage than curated baselines without explicit benchmark optimization, with continual improvements over time.

problem: Video generation models struggle with complex human movements because pixel-only training biases toward appearance over kinematic principles.
approach: EchoMotion extends diffusion transformers with dual-branch architecture processing video and motion tokens jointly, using MVS-RoPE for synchronized 3D positional encoding.
contribution: Constructs HuMoVe dataset of ~80k video-motion pairs and demonstrates that explicit motion representation improves complex human action video generation quality.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting fails in sparse-view settings due to geometric inaccuracies and sensitivity to camera trajectory smoothness.
approach: Proposes optimizing camera trajectories to maximize curvature coverage while enforcing smooth motion, combined with synthetic view generation.
contribution: Substantially outperforms state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks in sparse-view rendering quality and geometric fidelity while revealing implicit biases of 3DGS.

problem: Large vision-language models incur substantial computational overhead processing high-resolution images with many vision tokens.
approach: ERGO uses coarse-to-fine reasoning: downsampled image identifies task-relevant regions via reasoning-driven perception, then full-resolution crops are processed.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy than baseline models with competitive efficiency by leveraging multimodal context for region selection.

problem: Existing code reasoning benchmarks rely on synthetic/educational problems and coarse-grained tasks, failing to evaluate LLMs on real-world software engineering contexts.
approach: CodeSense constructs fine-grained semantic reasoning tasks from real repositories with execution traces as ground truth for Python, C, and Java.
contribution: First benchmark for fine-grained code semantic reasoning from real-world projects reveals fundamental gaps in LLM code comprehension despite prompting techniques.

problem: LLMs have inherent performance limitations that cannot be easily overcome during inference without model retraining.
approach: Dynamic Nested Depth reprocesses critical tokens identified by a router at transformer layers with controlled selection via router loss and threshold schemes.
contribution: Boosts dense models (Qwen3-1.7B/Llama3.2-1B/Gemma3-1B) by 1.88-2.61% and MoE models (Qwen3-30B) by 0.87% with minimal parameter/compute increase.

problem: Conformal prediction for LLM factuality guarantees relies on exchangeability assumptions violated by real-world distribution shifts.
approach: CoFact uses online density ratio estimation to adaptively reweigh calibration data, bypassing exchangeability and providing guarantees under distribution shift.
contribution: Maintains reliability under non-stationary conditions on MedLFQA, WikiData, and WildChat+ with asymptotic guarantee that hallucination rate gap approaches zero.

problem: Visible discontinuities in loss curves represent only a small fraction of actual breakthroughs in model learning, obscured by scalar loss metrics.
approach: POLCA decomposes training loss changes along low-rank subspace bases to identify clusters of samples with similar capability transitions.
contribution: Recovers interpretable phase transitions representing conceptual breakthroughs in both synthetic arithmetic and natural language tasks.

problem: Continual vision-language models struggle to maintain compositional structure while adapting to new domains with limited rehearsal budgets.
approach: Compo-ReAlign uses reversible composer for primitive-to-composition mapping, multi-positive InfoNCE for joint alignment, and spectral trust region for stability.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on compositional retrieval, improves over prior work by +2.4 R@1, and reduces forgetting by 40%.

problem: Neural network pruning plateaus around 50-60% sparsity for LLMs due to limitations in conventional surrogate-objective methods.
approach: Elsa uses ADMM-based constrained optimization without surrogate objectives, achieving 90% sparsity by identifying and addressing fundamental method limitations.
contribution: Achieves 7.8x less perplexity than best existing method on LLaMA-2-7B at 90% sparsity and enables 3.98x inference speedup with 7.80x memory compression.

problem: Vision-language models hallucinate due to perceptual bottlenecks in attended regions and insufficient visual robustness against image degradation.
approach: P2-DPO generates on-policy preference pairs targeting focus-and-enhance perception and visual robustness, with calibration loss aligning visual signals to text generation.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods using comparable training data on POPE and MMHal-Bench; validates improvements via attention region fidelity.

problem: Multi-task Bayesian optimization performance plateaus when scaling beyond moderate task counts due to shared-surrogate saturation.
approach: BOLT uses LLMs fine-tuned on prior BO runs to generate initialization candidates, maintaining single-task surrogates while creating closed-loop improvement.
contribution: Scales to ~1500 tasks without saturation; LLM initializations match or surpass from-scratch BO with far fewer oracle calls.

problem: Hyperparameter optimization for large-scale models requires separate searches at each scale, preventing efficient transfer across model dimensions.
approach: Extends CompleteP parameterization to transfer across width, depth, training horizon, and batch size using empirically validated scaling laws.
contribution: Demonstrates hyperparameter transfer holds per-layer and proposes simplified parameterization reducing search dimensionality without performance cost.

problem: Diffusion-based image editing entangles edited regions with global context, causing unintended modifications and poor instruction adherence.
approach: VAREdit reformulates editing as next-scale prediction with autoregressive models, using Scale-Aligned Reference module to inject scale-matched conditioning.
contribution: Outperforms diffusion methods on EMU-Edit and PIE-Bench in CLIP/GPT scores; completes 512x512 edits 2.2x faster than comparable methods.

problem: Vision-based 3D human motion capture ignores temporal consistency between frames, producing jittery motion due to Euler angle discontinuities.
approach: QuaMo uses quaternion differential equations and state-space models with adaptive meta-PD controller and quaternion geometric constraints.
contribution: Enables continuous 3D human kinematics estimation with no discontinuity and minimal artifacts compared to Euler-angle methods.

problem: Time-series forecasting models fail to handle concept drift (semantic shifts in underlying patterns), focusing only on temporal distribution shifts.
approach: ShifTS addresses temporal shift first via attention mechanisms finding invariant patterns, then applies soft attention for concept drift mitigation.
contribution: Method-agnostic framework consistently enhances forecasting accuracy across multiple datasets and outperforms dedicated concept/temporal drift baselines.

problem: Task and motion planning relies on manually-defined options (pick, place, move), limiting agent improvisation and discovery of novel behaviors.
approach: SLAP leverages model-free RL to learn shortcuts in the abstract planning graph induced by existing TAMP options.
contribution: Discovers dynamic improvisations (slap, wiggle, wipe) with 50% shorter plan lengths, outperforming planning and hierarchical RL baselines.

problem: Diffusion-based policy gradients require exact likelihood computation and bind to specific sampling methods, limiting applicability.
approach: FPO casts policy optimization as advantage-weighted flow matching loss compatible with PPO-clip, agnostic to integration method.
contribution: Trains diffusion-style policies from scratch capturing multimodal action distributions with higher performance than Gaussian policies in under-conditioned settings.

problem: Lane-level navigation requires expensive global HD maps but lacks the flexibility to adapt to dynamic road conditions from real-time perception.
approach: ONR refines SD-map routes to lane-level by associating with online perception maps using MAT transformer with path-aware and spatial attention.
contribution: Introduces OMA dataset (30K scenarios, 2.6M lane vectors) and demonstrates lane-level navigation with 34ms latency.

problem: Path imitation learning reduces navigation to memorizing single routes, limiting generalization and exploration of alternative valid paths.
approach: CompassNav shifts to Decision Understanding via RFT on Compass-Data-22k annotating all feasible actions with A* distances and gap-aware hybrid rewards.
contribution: 7B agent achieves state-of-the-art on navigation benchmarks, outperforms larger proprietary models, and succeeds on physical robot navigation.

problem: Token filtering in LLM training lacks real-world efficiency gains due to inadequate sparsity and incompatibility with standard ML libraries.
approach: Centrifuge filters activations in attention backward kernel to amplify sparsity and transforms sparse GEMM to dimension-reduced dense GEMM.
contribution: Reduces backpropagation time by up to 49.9% and end-to-end training by 34.7% when filtering 50% of tokens with 26.6% performance improvement.

problem: Vision-language-action models lack spatial awareness for 3D physical tasks because pretraining on 2D data without explicit 3D supervision.
approach: Spatial Forcing aligns intermediate visual embeddings with geometric representations from pretrained 3D foundation models without explicit 3D inputs.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art surpassing both 2D/3D baselines, accelerates training 3.8x, improves data efficiency across robotic tasks.

problem: Integral facility location with online learning advice lacks tight theoretical bounds unlike fractional versions.
approach: Presents first online rounding algorithms for facility location with applications to online settings enhanced with ML advice.
contribution: Establishes theoretical rounding guarantees for facility location under online learning-augmented conditions.

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning chains contain inaccurate statements that reduce performance and trustworthiness.
approach: Veracity Search performs discrete search over latent veracity assignments using LM likelihood as proxy reward; AVI learns amortized zero-shot inference.
contribution: Reliably identifies errors in logical, mathematical, and commonsense reasoning benchmarks with efficient inference-time verification.

problem: Optical projection inversion for screen exfiltration faces ill-posed inversion with singular Jacobian and irreversible light transport compression.
approach: IR4Net fuses Physically Regularized Irradiance Approximation with radiative transfer equation embedding and Irreversibility Constrained Semantic Reprojection.
contribution: Achieves reconstruction fidelity beyond neural methods while maintaining resilience to illumination perturbations on diverse scene categories.

problem: Vision Transformer knowledge distillation suffers from high-norm artifacts dominating the objective, causing students to underweight informative signals.
approach: SiNGER refines teacher features via nullspace-guided perturbation using LoRA-based adapters to suppress artifacts while preserving signals.
contribution: Consistently improves student models achieving state-of-the-art on downstream tasks with clearer, more interpretable representations.

problem: Multi-neuron convex relaxations for neural network certification may be incomplete, with unclear advantages over single-neuron methods.
approach: Provides first rigorous analysis showing multi-neuron relaxations are inherently incomplete but can achieve completeness via polynomial ReLU augmentation or polytope partitioning.
contribution: Establishes universal convex barrier for certification and characterizes distinguishing capabilities of multi-neuron over single-neuron approaches.

problem: Category-agnostic pose estimation assumes equal-weight edges in pose graphs, leading to suboptimal keypoint localization under occlusion.
approach: EdgeCape predicts edge weights in pose graphs and integrates Markov Attention Bias modulating self-attention by node hop distance.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on MP-100 benchmark in 1-shot and 5-shot settings with significantly improved keypoint accuracy.

problem: Protein language models scale poorly compared to NLP/vision models, plateauing at 650M-3B parameters despite larger pretraining.
approach: Reverse Distillation decomposes large model representations into orthogonal subspaces guided by smaller models matching protein property hierarchies.
contribution: Enables monotonic scaling with larger models consistently outperforming baselines while overcoming previous scaling plateaus on ProteinGym.

problem: LLMs exhibit limited Overton pluralism, failing to represent diverse viewpoints in outputs, with no scalable measurement approach.
approach: Formalizes Overton pluralism as set-coverage metric OVERTONSCORE via large-scale human study (N=1209) and develops automated benchmark reproducing judgments.
contribution: Models achieve 0.35-0.41 OVERTONSCORE far below theoretical maximum; automated benchmark achieves 0.88 rank correlation with human judgments.

problem: Object hallucination in multimodal LLMs is studied only with static benchmarks, missing model-specific vulnerabilities.
approach: GHOST optimizes image embeddings to induce hallucinations while keeping objects absent, using diffusion to generate natural-looking adversarial images.
contribution: Achieves 28% hallucination success rate versus 1% in prior methods; uncovers transferable vulnerabilities and validates fine-tuning as mitigation.

problem: Stop gradient and exponential moving average procedures in non-contrastive SSL avoid collapse without clear theoretical understanding.
approach: Analyzes from dual optimization and dynamical systems perspectives; shows these procedures don't optimize any smooth objective but characterize equilibria.
contribution: Proves in linear case that minimizing objective without stop gradient always leads to collapse; characterizes equilibria as asymptotically stable varieties.

problem: Personalized LLMs either overload context with all user history (costly/unscalable) or use one-shot similarity search missing deep context.
approach: RF-Mem implements dual-process memory retrieval: Familiarity for direct top-K via certainty, Recollection for iterative evidence expansion via α-mix.
contribution: Achieves scalable adaptive personalization avoiding full-context overhead across three benchmarks and corpus scales.

problem: Learned optimizers struggle to meta-generalize to unseen tasks, especially when scaling to wider networks than seen during training.
approach: Derives Maximal Update Parametrization for learned optimizer architectures with simple meta-training recipe for μ-parameterized LOs.
contribution: μLOs substantially improve meta-generalization to wider unseen tasks and show 5x generalization to deeper networks and 25x to longer horizons.

problem: Multi-modal dialogue systems lack rich datasets and struggle with conditional control over style and expressiveness across modalities.
approach: Introduces MM-Dia dataset (54.7k dialogues, 360+ hours) with fine-grained multi-modal annotations from movies/TV and MM-Dia-Bench for evaluation.
contribution: Demonstrates current frameworks' limitations in replicating human interaction expressiveness and provides benchmark for style-controllable dialogue.

problem: Multi-step generative models like diffusion require 40-100 function evaluations, limiting inference efficiency.
approach: TwinFlow trains 1-step generators via self-adversarial flows bypassing distillation and standard adversarial training complexity.
contribution: Achieves GenEval 0.83 at 1-NFE outperforming distillation baselines; scales to 20B multi-modal model with efficient few-step generation.

problem: Domain adaptive hashing transfers knowledge poorly due to target noise and indiscriminate domain alignment distorting features.
approach: Uses hierarchical conformal calibration with semantic-level confidence prediction sets and representation-level bit-level confidence for robust quantization.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements in cross-domain knowledge transfer with adaptive weighted Hamming distance retrieval.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Multi-agent visual reasoning systems either rely on single agents or hand-crafted pipelines without learning optimal agent selection.
approach: MATA presents hierarchical finite-state automaton where trainable hyper-agent selects states; agents use rule-based sub-automatons with shared memory.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on visual reasoning benchmarks with transparent execution via MATA-SFT-90K dataset for transition policy supervision.

problem: Large language models produce factually inconsistent content due to hallucination, limiting deployment in knowledge-intensive applications.
approach: NDAD identifies hallucination signals via selective attention head masking and subtracts mass from hallucination-prone output regions via gradient steps.
contribution: Enhances factual reliability across multiple LLMs and benchmarks without retraining or external knowledge requirements.
